meta.titre: Format of an informal letter in English

sections.contenu_markdown: A letter to a pen friend loses marks the moment it borrows the register of a formal business letter — the layout AND the tone must both stay informal.

An informal letter in English follows a fixed layout: sender's address (top right), date, an informal greeting ('Dear + first name'), an opening paragraph (reason for writing / polite enquiry), body paragraphs developing the main content, a closing paragraph, an informal closing formula ('Yours sincerely', 'Best wishes', etc.), and the sender's first name — never a formal 'Dear Sir/Madam' register.
sections.formule_principale: Address + Date / Dear [first name], / Opening / Body / Closing / Informal sign-off + first name

sections.enonce_markdown: Write the opening and closing of a letter to a pen friend named Tony, from Onana Blaise.

etapes.justification: State the reason for writing in a friendly tone.
etapes.resultat_markdown: I hope this letter finds you well...

etapes.justification: Use an informal sign-off and first name only.

sections.conclusion_markdown: A correctly formatted informal letter uses 'Dear [first name]' and an informal closing with the first name only, never a formal register.

items.erreur_markdown: Using 'Dear Sir/Madam' and 'Yours faithfully', the formal register reserved for business letters.
items.pourquoi_faux: A letter to a pen friend is a personal, informal communication; using a formal register is a register mismatch that examiners specifically penalise.
items.correction_markdown: Always match the register to the addressee: a friend gets 'Dear [first name]' / 'Yours sincerely' or 'Best wishes', never 'Dear Sir' / 'Yours faithfully'.

items.enonce_markdown: Which closing formula is correct for a letter to a pen friend: 'Yours faithfully' or 'Best wishes'?
items.solution_markdown: Best wishes (informal, appropriate to a personal letter).

items_markdown: Informal closing (Yours sincerely, Best wishes) + first name only
